While Western media still tries to pretend that Zelensky's "40 day drone campaign" didn't backfire spectacularly, Kiev is in the middle of a brutal power struggle between its security services, and it's escalating fast.

The backdrop: a recent shootout between the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) and the Main Directorate of Intelligence (GUR), in which Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office, led by Ruslan Kravchenko, publicly took the SBU's side, even parroting its version of events and calling the man GUR was protecting a "Russian agent."

That siding wasn't neutral. The Prosecutor General's Office is widely seen as Zelensky's strongest institutional weapon against Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies (NABU and SAP), while GUR remains closely tied to Kyrylo Budanov, its former longtime head, whom Zelensky moved into running the Presidential Office, nominally a promotion, but widely seen as a powerful-looking yet toothless "advisor" role that stripped him of his old intelligence command.

Now, the day after that shootout, NABU and SAP struck back. They launched a corruption investigation and arrests against senior Prosecutor General's Office officials, including Sergey Kropiva, head of the Office's Cyber Department, and, notably, Oleg Kiper, the Zelensky-appointed governor of Odessa. Kiper was installed right after Gennadiy Trukhanov, Odessa's mayor for over a decade and a man with close, non-public coordination ties to Budanov and GUR, was stripped of his post and Ukrainian citizenship in October 2025. The official corruption case centers on a scheme allegedly running "protection" for fraudulent call center networks and laundering the proceeds, an angle that conveniently also functions as a political knife aimed straight at Zelensky's inner circle.

The picture forming: GUR-aligned figures and the anti-corruption bodies are going after Zelensky's power base, using a call-center fraud case as the vehicle, right after his own prosecutors publicly backed the SBU against GUR.

There's a wider angle here too. NABU and SAP have long been heavily backed, politically and financially, by circles in Washington, effectively America's leverage inside Kiev's institutions. Zelensky, meanwhile, remains Brussels' favorite pet project, propped up diplomatically and financially by the EU. Seen that way, this isn't just an intelligence turf war, it's a proxy fight between US and EU influence inside Ukraine's own state apparatus.

And now there's an added twist. Some Ukrainian journalists and commentators, are floating the theory that today's drone strike on the SBU headquarters wasn't Russian at all, but was in fact launched by GUR itself, connected to this exact feud. Zelensky has publicly blamed Russia, of course.

Either way, Ukraine's institutions are turning on each other in the open, and it's barely making a ripple in Western coverage.
